title: Capacity Swap Window Runbook — April 2026
content:
Purpose
This runbook documents a planned ‘capacity swap’ maintenance approach for April 2026 where we temporarily shift/repurpose GPU capacity across regions to create windows for driver upgrades, firmware patching, and emergency kernel fixes with minimal impact to customer latency SLOs. The approach reduces full-fleet drains by creating short, predictable windows and localized headroom via cross-region surge and transient routing.

Scope
- Affects hosted API + Dedicated pools in regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1.
- Applies to NVIDIA driver updates (R515->R525 family), kernel micropatches, and NVSwitch firmware where required.
- Does NOT include major model migrations or re-quant builds; those are separate change windows.

High-level strategy
1) Pre-create surge capacity in a partner region by briefly reducing non-critical burst capacity and shifting some model-serving traffic to compatible model variants with slightly higher latency but same quality profile.
2) Label and cordon target hosts for maintenance and perform driver upgrades in small batches (4–8 GPUs at a time per AZ).
3) Reintroduce GPUs and run validation traffic; if green, re-balance traffic back.
4) Repeat until region complete.

Why ‘capacity swap’ vs full drain
- Full-fleet drains create long outages and high risk to latency SLOs.
- Swap uses temporary surge capacity and traffic steering to preserve tail latency while maintenance proceeds faster in parallel across multiple small batches.
- Reduces risk of needing emergency rollback and reduces overall maintenance wall-clock by 25–40% in internal simulations.

Pre-maintenance checklist (72–48 hours out)
- Confirm maintenance window with PMs and support: 4-hour windows per region, with 2 hours of aggressive probing and 2 hours of conservative verification.
- Freeze non-essential deployments to target pools for window duration (release-engineering action).
- Update routing policy: add canary route rules to shift up to 18% of traffic away from target region and allow for traffic surge to destination regions.
- Provision surge instances: ensure at least 10% spare capacity in destination regions (platform-engineering to confirm).
- Validate model compatibility: solutions-engineering to ensure top 20 models can run on alternative variant (same token costs and semantic tests).
- Notify customers and set status page messages: customer-success lead to draft communication.
- Run preflight job: kernel/module version check, GPU health baseline, KV cache checkpoint.

Maintenance window plan (detailed timeline)
- T-0: Start shift-out phase (00:00–00:30) — route 12–18% of steady-state QPS away to destination regions and to compatible model variants. Monitor 95/99 latency and error rate.
- T+30: Cordon first host-group A (4 GPUs) and begin driver install (00:30–01:00). Health probes unchanged except we lower capacity threshold on pool by 3% to allow transient spikes.
- T+60: Uncordon host-group A after validation (smoke generation of 1000 requests per model class). If validation passes, restore 2–3% of capacity.
- T+90: Cordon next host-group B (4 GPUs) and repeat.
- Repeat batches until region complete.
- Final T+240: Complete traffic normalization (00:00–04:00 window) and run a region-level soak test for 1 hour.

Batch size guidance and constraints
- Default batch: 4 GPUs per AZ (safe default for p4d-style machines).
- Max simultaneous cordons per region: 2 batches (to keep headroom).
- If baseline utilization > 70% steady-state in a region, reduce batch size to 2 GPUs and require additional surge capacity.

Traffic routing and fallback rules
- Primary method: policy-based smart routing using cost/latency tier. For the window, temporarily bump route weight to destination regions for requests with latency slack metadata, up to the pre-agreed QPS cap.
- Fallback: if destination region 99p latency breaches 350ms for >5 min, rollback routing to prior weight and abort further cordons until stable.
- Automatic failover: if host-level errors spike >1% for any 10-minute window during a batch, immediately stop cordoning and return traffic.

Validation suite (post-upgrade)
- Smoke tests: token-level generation verification, KV cache warmup, end-to-end latency against synthetic profiles.
- Functional tests: top-10 customer prompt tests for semantic drift, for all shifted model variants.
- Resource tests: check CUDA driver logs for silent errors, GPU ECC counters, PCI resets.
- Observability checks: ensure tracing tags propagate and sampling rates match pre-maintenance baselines.

Rollback criteria and playbook
- Immediate rollback if any of these occur during a batch: 10% increase in 99p latency, >2% error rate increase, failing semantic tests for any golden prompt.
- Rollback steps: remove driver changes on affected hosts (if rollback supported), or drain and replace with healthy instance from pre-validated image. Inform customers and update status.

Communication plan
- Pre-window: status page + email to active enterprise customers 48h prior. Slack #infra-maintenance-threads updated at T-24, T-6.
- During window: hourly check-ins on Slack with short summary (batches completed / failed / remediation). Pager escalations to oncall if >1 batch fails.
- Post-window: summary doc with runtime metrics, regressions found, and action items within 48h.

Safety & risk mitigations
- Canary on <1% traffic before first full batch.
- Small batches and automatic stop rules.
- Holdback pool: 6–8 GPUs per region reserved as instant replacements.
- Runbook dry-run in staging 7 days prior (same topology as production but scaled down) and collect run metrics.

Operational run notes (tips from previous runs)
- Stagger maintenance start times across regions by at least 90 minutes to give SRE time to respond to early anomalies.
- Prefer driver families that have been validated with our kernel build matrix; avoid mixing experimental drivers in the same window.
- Use synthetic traffic that matches tail percentiles, not just average QPS.

Appendix: quick commands and queries
- Fleet state: infra-cli fleet list --region <region> --tag maintenance
- Cordon host: infra-cli host cordon --host-id <id>
- Apply driver: infra-cli host exec --host-id <id> --cmd "sudo dpkg -i /opt/drivers/nvidia-525*.deb"
- Smoke test run: jobs-cli run --job maintenance-smoke --region <region> --batch <id>

Open questions / decisions pending
- Final surge region: eu-west-1 vs us-east-1 (ops preference is eu-west-1; finance prefers us-east-1 due to lower egress costs).
- Acceptable customer QPS cap for diverted traffic; propose 18% but product to sign-off.

Owner & next steps
- Owner: Priya Menon (infra capacity planner) — action: finalize surge region and schedule dry-run.
- Action items for next week: validate top-20 model compatibility (solutions-engineering), confirm spare capacity in destination regions (platform-engineering), draft customer-facing message (customer-success).

This document is a working runbook; expect edits from SRE, platform, and product teams. Save major changes as new versions and record post-mortem metrics after completion.
